lessonTitle: How the impact of Medical Affairs is measured

slides.title: Medical Affairs Has No Clean Success Proxy
bullets: Commercial has sales volume and market share as a direct proxy
Medical Affairs should not create an equivalent metric
A sales-like number would compromise its independence

slides.title: Activity Counts Don't Prove Impact
bullets: Relied on KOL interaction counts, requests answered, publications supported
Counting interactions says nothing about whether they changed anything
Activity volume and impact are simply not the same thing

slides.title: Outcome-Based KPIs Tied to Patient Care
bullets: Tracks insights that were actually acted upon, not just logged
Measures clinical practice or guideline changes field engagement contributed to
Tracks downstream use of evidence: citations, guideline inclusion, HTA submissions

slides.title: Qualitative Assessment Answers the Harder Question
bullets: Structured KOL feedback and internal stakeholder satisfaction
Documented case studies of insight-to-action pathways
Quantitative shows how much was done; qualitative shows whether it mattered

slides.title: Build Impact on Traceable Outcomes, Not Visit Counts
bullets: Don't lean primarily on how many visits you completed
Build a small number of well-documented insight-to-outcome examples
This is the evidence a modern Medical Affairs organisation looks for

takeaway.title: Impact in Medical Affairs is proven through traceable outcomes and qualitative value, not activity counts
bullets: Activity metrics like visit counts don't prove anything actually changed
Outcome-based KPIs track insights acted upon and evidence used downstream
Build your own case for impact on a few well-documented outcomes
